question: to the Commission Yannis Maniatis (S&D) Subject:

During a committee hearing in the Greek Parliament, the CEO of the Hellenic Railways Organisation (OSE) revealed that the centralised traffic control and automatic braking system, ETCS, is not yet operational anywhere along the Greek railway network, despite the Prime Minister’s announcements in April 2025 that it would be operational by September 2025 at the latest. It is worth remembering that the first contract for the installation of the ETCS system was signed in 2014 and the installation should have been completed by 2016. As acknowledged by the special committee set up to investigate the Tempi train crash in 2023, if the system had been operational, the collision of the two trains would have been avoided. Since the installation of the ETCS was financed by the European Union, and its operation is an essential prerequisite for transport safety, can the Commission answer the following: 1.

Has the Greek Government informed the Commission about when the ETCS system is expected to operate properly and fully, and has it provided an explanation for the threeyear delay following the Tempi tragedy and the constant government announcements?
Is Greece meeting its rail safety obligations even though the ETCS is not operational?
What measures will the Commission take to ensure the safety of rail transport in Greece?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (15.9.2026) The Commission remains in contact with the Greek authorities in relation to the modernisation and reform of its railway sector, including deployment of the European Railway Traffic Management System (ERTMS). The Commission is aware of the ambitious ERTMS roll-out plans. Given the complexity of this process, the European Union Agency for Railways (ERA), at the request of Greece, is supporting stakeholders in developing an effective ERTMS deployment plan. Railway safety can be achieved through a combination of different technical and organisational measures. The deployment on the rail network of European Train Control System (ETCS), a key component of ERTMS, contributes to the improvement of safety of the railway system; however, railway networks can also safely operate without ETCS, provided that appropriate alternative risk control measures are implemented. On 16 December 2024, the Commission opened infringement proceedings (INFR(2023)20361) against Greece for failure to comply with the requirements of the Rail Safety Directive2. The infringement case addresses several long-standing systemic shortcomings in the implementation of the Safety Directive in Greece, also identified during an audit by ERA. In response to the audit report, the Greek authorities have prepared in 2024 an Action Plan to address these shortcomings, which is being implemented, and the Commission is monitoring progress on the basis of regular reports received from Greece.
1 Press release: https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/inf_24_6006. 2 Directive (EU) 2016/798 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 May 2016 on railway safety
